title: The founder planning a move
subtitle: Incorporation and permission to work are separate
prompt: I'm a German founder living in Berlin. I want a Delaware company and plan to spend six months in the US building the product and meeting investors. Can I do that on a visitor visa once I own the company? I haven't decided between an LLC and a corporation.
provided: Plans about six months in the US
Activities include product development and investor meetings
Assumes ownership may permit work on visitor status
missing: Actual immigration status and proposed travel dates
Detailed planned activities in the US
Prior US presence and tax-residency facts
Owners, financing plans, and intended work locations
Existing German business and management arrangements

questions.question: What activities will you perform in the US, for whom, and under which current or proposed status?
questions.why: Meetings and active product work require different immigration analysis.

questions.question: What are the proposed travel dates and your US presence during the prior two years?
questions.why: Tax-residency analysis is distinct from immigration permission and is not a simple six-month rule.

questions.question: Will you have cofounders or external investors, and have they specified a structure?
questions.why: Entity selection should follow the ownership and financing facts.

questions.question: Will a German business, home office, team, or management role continue after the move?
questions.why: Local residence and company treatment require German advice.

questions.question: Which commitments depend on traveling, starting work, or issuing equity, and when?
questions.why: Identify sequencing decisions to take to counsel before commitments.

concerns.title: Ownership does not settle work authorization
concerns.detail: Visitor guidance distinguishes permitted business visits from employment or work. Counsel must assess the actual product-development plan.

concerns.title: Tax residency needs its own timeline
concerns.detail: Evaluate substantial presence, green-card status, exceptions, and any relevant treaty facts separately.

concerns.title: Entity choice remains open
concerns.detail: Clarify owners and intended classification before preparing formation documents.

specialists.decision: Assess permitted activities, available routes, and timing before the founder works or travels.
specialists.needs: Status documents, activity plan, travel history and financing facts

specialists.decision: Assess residence, entity classification, management, and cross-border reporting.
specialists.needs: Day counts, residence ties, management arrangements and business records

takeaway: Resolve the work and travel plan alongside the company structure.
